messages.body_plain:
:-)  Sounds like your problem is not the conversion, but validation of the new file. I am not sure how anyone who isn't familiar with your dataset can help.  If some one else do the conversion in a different method, he will still be susceptible to the same mistakes (or other mistakes).
Maybe a better course of action is that you should validate the converted data, Maybe by comparing for some observations in the original db or thinking about axioms you know should hold in this data and see if they are not skewed....

messages.subject: a little help to an ole hadash
messages.subject_clean: a little help to an ole hadash
messages.body_plain:
Dear R users,
In a couple of months I am going to make aliyah and am now looking for a job in Israel. I am 27, in September 2017 will get my PhD in Mathematical Biology (will have to return back to Moscow for the defense). Since R is my main weapon, I am looking for the labs which use R as their programming tool. My area of interests includes data analysis for biology, statistical modelling, biostatistics and so on. If, by any chance, anyone is interested in me, my CV is attached.

Thus, the question is: can anyone reference a work group in Israel that works on applied maths and/or computational biology and uses R?
If anyone can help me or knows anyone who can help -- please, tell me, I'll be most grateful.

!שבוע טוב לכולם
Dmitry
